newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Part of Yugo privatisation funds to be reinvested.
newsitem.headline: Part of Yugo privatisation funds to be reinvested.

text.p: Part of the capital raised from the privatisation of Yugoslavia's state-owned enterprises will be reinvested in the firms, Serbia's Industry Minister Oskar Fodor said on Thursday
Addressing a symposium of 400 Yugoslav financial and economic experts he said all money from the sale of state enterprises would go into a state-owned development fund.
"The development fund will have to reinvest part of the money from the sales in the same enterprise. The fund will also provide loans under very favourable conditions," he said.
"In this way we want to attract foreign investors to buy part of or entire enterprises. The investors will be able to get the money from the fund as working capital," he added.
Fodor also ruled out the idea, which had been circulating, of issuing vouchers to workers in enterprises being privatised which could be exchanged for shares after a certain period.
"There will be no voucher privatisation in Serbia," he said, adding that workers would be able to buy shares in their companies at a discount.
The Serbian government is in the process of drafting a privatisation law which is due to be submitted to parliament in early autumn.
Under the law an enterprise's board of directors will have to decide if and when an enterprise should be privatised, and determine its value within a year.
He said Serbia would have some problems with large state enterprises that were used to being cushioned by the government.
"It will not be possible to privatise big systems so
easily, and the government is searching for the best solutions in this process of transition and privatisation," he said.
The minister said that about 5,000 private enterprises had come up with good investment programmes to build small factories with the help of foreign capital.
"We have to let them breathe and not choke them with high taxes," Fodor said.
